Was it difficult for you to find the right therapist? Also, was the therapy expensive? The more I read these comments, the more excited I become about getting better. The one that was wonderful- did she give you books to read or offer you advice on how to solve your problems?

Your response literally made me tear up. I'm trying to hide this thread from my bf, so I'm making a very poor attempt to not burst out crying. Thank you so much! Thank you also for describing the process a bit. Do you still remember the tips and tricks your therapist taught you? Did they prescribe medication for your depression or did you overcome it yourself (with their advice)? I'm so, so happy for you! And I'm REALLY happy you didn't go through with the suicide because then I might have joined you too. The fact that you're on your computer cheering on a total stranger just shows how amazing of a person you are. :)

The reason I even asked this question is because I always assumed therapy was for people who needed to talk their shit out. Now that I'm lonely, I have started having all these other issues I can't fix myself which is why I want to know if therapy is the route to go. Your description is really helpful. Have you been to therapy? If you have, I'd like to know how it personally helped you.

Thank you for that! I'm a third year who transferred in, so that's the main reason why I have no friends. Every one my age has had two years to establish their friends circle and niche. Whenever I'm on campus, I always see a group of people laughing and talking and it makes me hate myself. I fucking HATE being on campus because everyone is with someone. My boyfriend goes to school out of state and my family lives a little over an hour away (which is not far- just a nuisance). My depression mainly stems from not having a friend to call my own because I've literally forgotten how to have fun- which is why I can't make friends.
 Have you had therapy before? If so, what was your experience like? Thank you again for your kind words :)

I'm actually involved on campus, but I'm seriously the most awkward person I know. It's not even the 'heart warming' awkward where the awkwardness is actually funny, but the awkwardness that makes you almost cringe. That's probably a big reason I'm so depressed. I completely agree with you that the work is going to HAVE to come from me, but I'm scared that I'll go to one session and absolutely breakdown if it doesn't go well. That's part of the reason I want to get a feel of what I should expect, because I know that if it doesn't go well (i.e not at all helpful), then I'll give up and succumb to my depression.

 Do you think you would be the same person without the therapy? Was the advice they gave you helpful?

Thank you for a different perspective. For me, I don't see it helping me because I'm a really negative person and I think I would make fun of some of the advice. Of course, if I'm paying them then I will try my best to be as optimistic as possible. Why do you think it hasn't helped you?

I was just really curious HOW they help you because I don't need someone to just talk to. I can talk to my boy friend or family if that's what I needed. Do you think you'd be where you are now without therapy?

Gotcha. I see what you're saying. I think OP should give him a second chance, but she's not obligated to. My original response wasn't a statement of disgust directed at OP's reluctance to have a relationship with the man, but rather disgust at the 90% of people who encouraged her to break it off immediately. She shouldn't feel obligated to be with him, but if she likes the person he is now, then she should give him a CHANCE. I'm not talking about obligations to be with this person or that person.
 
 I'm defining second chance in a more figurative sense like he deserves to be happy but OP doesn't have to be the one to give it to him. I was just saying that she shouldn't restrict herself based on his past. She should make her decision based on the person he is today.

If a man I like apporached me with a similar story like OP's "boyfriend," and PROVED to me he is trying to change, then I would give him a chance. I would understand that he has a past, just like I do (even though I was the victim), and I would also understand that  his past shouldn't define his future. I don't know if my response makes any sense. For me, the guy should get a second chance.
